items_all.title: Anthropic's Claude can now orchestrate up to 1,000 AI agents in parallel through dynamic workflows
items_all.summary: Anthropic is adding dynamic workflows to Claude Managed Agents, letting a lead agent distribute tasks across up to 1,000 sub-agents at once. In testing, a single agent found at most 27 of 70 hidden bugs in a codebase, while the multi-agent workflow consistently caught 66. The article Anthropic's Claude can now orchestrate up to 1,000 AI agents in parallel through dynamic workflows appeared first on The Decoder .
items_all.summary_zh: Anthropic 正在為 Claude 受管理代理程式（Managed Agents）新增動態工作流程，讓主代理程式能夠同時將任務分配給多達 1,000 個子代理程式。在測試中，單一代理程式在程式碼庫中最多隻能找到 70 個隱藏錯誤中的 27 個，而多代理程式工作流程則能持續抓出 66 個。文章 Anthropic's Claude 透過動態工作流程，現在可以平行編排多達 1,000 個 AI 代理程式，最早出現於 The Decoder。

items_all.title: Anthropic launches a free AI scanner for open-source projects
items_all.summary: Anthropic has launched "Cyber Mission," a program to protect critical infrastructure and open-source software from cyberattacks. Partners like CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks will help secure power grids and water systems, while a free AI scanner automatically checks open-source projects for vulnerabilities with an expected accuracy above 90 percent. The article Anthropic launches a free AI scanner for open-source projects appeared first on The Decoder .
items_all.summary_zh: Anthropic 推出了「網路任務」（Cyber Mission），這是一項旨在保護關鍵基礎設施和開源軟體免受網路攻擊的計畫。CrowdStrike 和 Palo Alto Networks 等合作夥伴將協助保護電網和供水系統的安全，而免費的 AI 掃描器則會自動檢查開源專案中的漏洞，預期準確度超過 90%。本文 Anthropic launches a free AI scanner for open-source projects 最初發表於 The Decoder。

items_all.title: OpenAI revenue keeps surging as company seeks $30 billion in fresh capital

The correction sent chip stocks sliding. Meanwhile, OpenAI is negotiating at least $30 billion in fresh capital at a $1.4 trillion valuation. The article OpenAI revenue keeps surging as company seeks $30 billion in fresh capital appeared first on The Decoder .
items_all.summary_zh: OpenAI's 的年化營收率約為 50 會億美元，遠低於先前根據不同會計方法所報導的 70 億美元數據。這項修正導致晶片股下跌。同時，OpenAI 正在洽談以 1.4 兆美元的估值籌集至少 300 億美元的新資金。這篇題為 OpenAI revenue keeps surging as company seeks $30 billion in fresh capital 的文章最初發表於 The Decoder 。

items_all.summary: Deno is joining Cloudflare The Deno team released the first version of celld back in August - their open source implementation of the Durable Objects pattern from Cloudflare Workers. Today, Cloudflare are acquiring Deno outright, with the goal of building on celld to "make workerd self-hosting a first-class supported way to build and run apps using the Workers programming model" (see the Cloudflare blog .) The bad news is that Deno itself will not be maintained by Cloudflare beyond the next year: We will support the Deno runtime for another year with monthly releases containing bug fixes and security updates. After that year we will end our development of the Deno runtime. Deno will remain open source, and we welcome others who want to continue its development. Deno (and Node.js) creator Ryan Dahl explained that decision in a comment on Hacker News: It's a joint decision and I agree with it. I'm most invested in its success and have put the most work into it - and I no longer think it's where I can do the most important work. items_all.summary: I shipped a new feature for my blog today: the Newsletters page, which offers an index of all of the newsletters I've sent out, both my free weekly Substack and my monthly sponsors-only updates. I built the feature almost entirely using my voice, chatting away to my laptop while I cooked dinner. Codex voice mode I used the ChatGPT desktop app for this, in the Codex tab, using the voice conversation mode, running against a local development environment. Here's what that looks like: I started the session against my local simonwillisonblog checkout by typing: Start dev server and open in browser This gave me a preview of the site that it would be working on, and meant that I could later ask it to show me the new pages so I could visually track its progress. Then I clicked the "Start new voice chat" button - that's not the microphone button, it's the one to the right of it - and set my laptop up in the kitchen so I could talk to it while I cooked. Talking to my computer I had a pretty good idea of what I wanted to build, and it's a simple enough Django feature that I was certain the model (in this case GPT-6 Astra High) would be able to do it. A new model, a migration, some view code, templates, and a couple of import functions to populate the database from external sources. items_all_raw.title: Deno is joining Cloudflare
items_all_raw.summary: Deno is joining Cloudflare The Deno team released the first version of celld back in August - their open source implementation of the Durable Objects pattern from Cloudflare Workers. Today, Cloudflare are acquiring Deno outright, with the goal of building on celld to "make workerd self-hosting a first-class supported way to build and run apps using the Workers programming model" (see the Cloudflare blog .) The bad news is that Deno itself will not be maintained by Cloudflare beyond the next year: We will support the Deno runtime for another year with monthly releases containing bug fixes and security updates. After that year we will end our development of the Deno runtime. Deno will remain open source, and we welcome others who want to continue its development. Deno (and Node.js) creator Ryan Dahl explained that decision in a comment on Hacker News: It's a joint decision and I agree with it. I'm most invested in its success and have put the most work into it - and I no longer think it's where I can do the most important work. There are some good ideas in Deno and it's well engineered - but it ultimately is not solving big problems. It has been sucked into the gravity well of node compatibility, which forces it to behave exactly as Node does. Why reimplement Node? It works. items_all_raw.title: A new feature for my blog, built using my voice
items_all_raw.summary: I shipped a new feature for my blog today: the Newsletters page, which offers an index of all of the newsletters I've sent out, both my free weekly Substack and my monthly sponsors-only updates. I built the feature almost entirely using my voice, chatting away to my laptop while I cooked dinner. Codex voice mode I used the ChatGPT desktop app for this, in the Codex tab, using the voice conversation mode, running against a local development environment. Here's what that looks like: I started the session against my local simonwillisonblog checkout by typing: Start dev server and open in browser This gave me a preview of the site that it would be working on, and meant that I could later ask it to show me the new pages so I could visually track its progress. Then I clicked the "Start new voice chat" button - that's not the microphone button, it's the one to the right of it - and set my laptop up in the kitchen so I could talk to it while I cooked. Talking to my computer I had a pretty good idea of what I wanted to build, and it's a simple enough Django feature that I was certain the model (in this case GPT-6 Astra High) would be able to do it. A new model, a migration, some view code, templates, and a couple of import functions to populate the database from external sources.
